task.title: Verify desktop changes in CI without running the Go matrix
task.description:
Give `desktop/` its own verification, and keep a change confined to it from spending the Go matrix.

Depends on the move; the job has nothing to run until the source is here.

## Reuse the mechanism that already exists

`ci.yml` already solved this shape for `site/`, and the reasoning in it applies unchanged:

> The obvious fix, `paths-ignore` on the triggers, is the wrong one here. `Verify on ubuntu-24.04` and `Verify on macos-15` are required status checks, and a run that never starts never reports them, so a site-only pull request would wait forever on a check GitHub was never going to send. The job therefore keeps triggering on everything and keeps reporting; only the expensive steps below are skipped.

A `desktop/`-only change takes that same path: the verification job still triggers and still reports, and the expensive steps skip. A Go-only change skips the desktop job by the same rule.

Every uncertainty resolves to "run everything", as it does today: an unknown event, a missing base commit, a force push, a failed diff and an empty diff all decide to verify.

## What the desktop job runs

Workbench's existing checks, which are cheap and several of which are the kind this repository already likes. They ran in Workbench's own `ci.yml`, which the move deletes rather than carries, so this task ports them into the root `ci.yml`:

- every renderer class the shell applies is actually styled (`desktop/scripts/check-styles.js`);
- every export of every main-process module is defined;
- the renderer references only element ids that exist;
- IPC channels invoked by the preload are handled by the main process;
- every source file parses (`node --check`).

Node 22 and `npm ci` in `desktop/`. The Go test for `desktop/scripts/build-workbook.sh` that the move adds under `scripts/` runs with the Go matrix, since that is where it lives; the desktop job runs only the Node checks.

## One check that does not come across

Workbench's CI verified that a generated dark-mode overlay still matched its source. The move deletes the overlay, its generator and that check; the board has a dark mode of its own since #131 and #132.

comments.author: a@example.com
comments.body: https://github.com/dgoings/workbook/pull/137: desktop_changed as a second output of the existing gate; Node, npm ci and npm run check as gated steps inside the single Verify job on the Ubuntu runner. Not a separate job: the workflow's own tests forbid one because the required checks must always report. Gate logic proven locally by the workflow tests against fixture repositories.
